subject: pe
title: Fitts & Posner Learning Stages
welcome_lead: Cognitive, associative, autonomous — three stages of motor learning.
meta_desc: A-Level PE adventure on Fitts & Posner stages and feedback types.
final_note: Each stage needs different practice and feedback — coach the stage you face.

concepts.def: Beginner; trial-and-error, high attentional demand (Fitts & Posner 1967).
Practice phase; smoother performance, errors decline.
Skill executed with minimal conscious attention.
Information from athlete's own senses (proprioception, vision).

walkthroughs.body_html: Cognitive: thinking through every move. Associative: refining. Autonomous: 'automatic' execution.
Cognitive learners need frequent extrinsic feedback. Autonomous learners benefit from sparse, summary feedback.
Massed, repetitive practice suits early stages; distributed and variable practice supports retention later.

mcqs.q: The autonomous stage of learning is characterised by:
options: Skill execution with minimal conscious attention
Information the performer senses from their own body during/after movement.

mcqs.q: Is a tennis serve a closed or open skill?
options: Closed - performed in a predictable, self-paced environment.
Open - because tennis is a fast-paced sport.
